newsitem.title: USA: ConEd to restore NY nuke a week after meeting.
newsitem.headline: ConEd to restore NY nuke a week after meeting.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said Friday it expects to restore its Indian Point 2 nuclear power unit within a week after a meeting with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) next Wednesday.
"We expect to come back on line within a week after the NRC (meeting)," said ConEd spokeswoman Joan Burger.
In its Friday daily plant report, NRC provided a tentative restart date fo Feb 23 for Indian Point 2.
The Wednesday meeting is a key step required by the NRC before ConEd can restart the Indian Point 2 unit.
"The topic of discussion will be about the investigation we have conducted on the cause of the feedwater regulatory valves," Burger said.
She said they would also discuss the corrective actions ConEd has taken during the outage.
The 975 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 2 along the Hudson River north of New York City was shut January 27 to repair problems that caused the feedwater valve to become inoperable.

Subsequent investigations by ConEd pointed to debris in the unit's feedwater and condensate systems as the culprit behind valve problem, a NRC spokeswoman said, adding ConEd also discovered debris in the systems in June 1995.
